sentence: This project measures how strong the small magnet inside one electron and one positron is, to test the Standard Model.
This project tests a method that injects low energy ions into thin sheets of material to add other atoms without damaging it.
This project studies how construction workers can learn to work safely with robots, using virtual reality training.
This project builds a system that shows 3D human motion remotely so expert care can reach people doing rehabilitation.
This project builds a toolkit that makes quantum computers easier for scientists to use, starting with a geophysical application.
This project builds deep learning models of the atmosphere and tests how stable and reliable they are for predicting extreme weather.
This project runs a research center on financial technology that works with industry on problems using artificial intelligence and quantum computing.
This project studies how chemical bonds in crystalline compounds with a square net of atoms shape their electronic and magnetic properties.
This project studies how one protein helps cells change their arrangement as the eye of fruit flies develops.
This project studies the bacteria living with microalgae in corals and tests whether they improve algal thermal tolerance.
This project builds hands-on labs and curricular modules that teach how to keep quantum computing systems secure and private.
This project uses mass spectrometry to identify microorganisms, including drug-resistant ones, and studies how environments like streams and lakes contribute to antimicrobial resistance.
This project looks for the genes on unique chromosomes that determine whether a plant is male or female and uses them to engineer artificial chromosomes.
This project builds a secure timing system for edge systems with different clocks, including ways to share time that resist delay attacks.
This project builds a programming practice tool that uses AI to pick practice questions and write feedback that fit each learner.
This project builds annotated datasets of endangered languages and tests computer techniques that work when only small amounts of data exist.
This project uses iron-loving elements in meteorites and mantle-derived materials to find out what the building blocks of Earth were made of.
